reason: The draft answers Nessa's question directly and honestly: no running every day. It explains why in terms a beginner can follow (tendons and feet adapt during rest) and gives a clear path forward (more running within each session first, then a fourth day later). It keeps her Mon/Wed/Sat routine and her dog walks, so it fits her life. The increase is small: 25 and 25 minutes of 1:1 walk-run, then 30 minutes at 90:60 on Saturday. That is a reasonable step from roughly 2.3 km per session. It isn't a sharp jump in volume or long run. Her calf tightness clears within a day, which is normal adaptation and not an injury sign, so no referral was needed. Every day can be run as written. It loses a point for three things. The calf flag says "watch" but never says what to do if the tightness lasts longer or gets sharp. The heart-rate caps assume she has a monitor and has no basis in her card. And it never links the plan to the 15 November race timeline, which was the goal behind her question.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Strong first week, and the smartest next step is to keep the same three run days and nudge them a touch longer, not add more. …
Answers: (1) No, please do not run every day next week. Your legs, tendons and feet are still meeting running for the first time, and the gains come while you rest between sessions, not during them. (2) Three run days with a rest or walk day in between is the right dose for now. We will grow the time you spend running inside each session first, then add a fourth day later in the block when that feels easy.
Safety flag: Watch the calves across the week
Next week:
Mon: easy, 25 min walk-run, 1 min run and 1 min walk repeated, heart rate under 150…
Tue: rest, dog walk only, easy pace. Lets the calves settle before the next run.
Wed: easy, 25 min walk-run, 1 min run and 1 min walk repeated, heart rate under 150…
Thu: rest, dog walk only, easy pace. Keeps you moving without loading the legs.
Fri: rest, full day off or a short gentle walk. Freshens you up for the longer Saturday…
Sat: easy, 30 min walk-run, 90 sec run and 60 sec walk repeated, heart rate under 155…
Sun: rest, dog walk only, easy pace. Recovery after the longest session of the week.
